prior_importants.description: The sandbox denyWrite list names the main `.git`'s `config` and `config.worktree` but not `config.lock` / `config.worktree.lock`, while it does deny `packed-refs.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `index.lock` and `main.lock`. Git commits a config write by renaming `config.lock` over `config`, so content a worker puts into the lock lands in the main config.

The sandbox allows `registry.yarnpkg.com`, and pup's TypeScript adapter treats a repo with `yarn.lock` as a yarn project, but WORKER_CACHE_VARS redirects only npm, pip, uv and poetry. Yarn 4's global cache (`~/.yarn/berry/cache`) is outside every grant, so a sandboxed install that misses the cache fails with EPERM.

findings.description: SYMLINK_CHECK_SHELL walks the sed-normalized `$REL` (`LINK_REST=$REL`), but the Write tool opens the raw `file_path`. sed works line by line, so its `s#^\./##` strip also fires after an embedded newline, where it is not a path-equivalent rewrite. A sandboxed worker plants a symlink whose name ends in `<LF>.` and then Writes through it. The hook checks a different, nonexistent path, exits 0 on scope-in, and the unsandboxed Write follows the link to a compiled hook or to the main checkout's `.pupitre/project.yml`.
findings.body:
**A newline in `file_path` gets a Write past the new symlink check, which reopens the escape the check was added to close.**

The walk runs on `REL` after it has been normalized, not on the path Edit or Write will actually open:

```sh
FILE=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
...
REL=$(printf '%s' "$REL" | sed -e 's#//*#/#g' -e ':a' -e 's#/\./#/#g; s#^\./##' -e 'ta')
...
LINK_PATH=$WORKTREE
LINK_REST=$REL
```

sed works one line at a time, so `^\./` also matches right after an embedded LF. For `src/evil<LF>./project.yml`, the kernel resolves the components `src`, `evil<LF>.` and `project.yml`. sed rewrites the path to `src/evil<LF>project.yml`, which has a different set of components.

**Trigger (`workerSandbox: true`):**
1. Sandboxed Bash creates a link in the worktree: `ln -s <main>/.pupitre "src/$(printf 'evil\n.')"`. The target could also be the session's compiled `hooks/` dir.
2. The worker calls Write with `file_path` = `<worktree>/src/evil\n./project.yml`.
3. In the hook:
   - The worktree-prefix `case`, the `/../` check and the `^\.claude/` check all pass, because `*` matches a newline.
   - The walk tests `src`, which is a real dir, then `src/evil<LF>project.yml`, which does not exist, so it `break`s. The real link is never tested.
   - `printf '%s\n' "$REL" | grep -qE -f scope-in.pat` passes when any one line matches, and `src/evil` matches `src/**`.
4. Write runs outside the sandbox and follows the link. It can rewrite `project.yml` to turn `workerSandbox` off for later launches, or overwrite a compiled hook that then runs unsandboxed.

A trailing newline does the same without sed: `$(...)` strips trailing LFs from `FILE`. Whether the Write tool keeps a trailing LF is Claude Code internals and was not probed. The embedded variant does not depend on it.

ADR 0191 says the hook refuses such a link "short of the race in ceiling 14". This bypass involves no race, and no ceiling covers it.

**Fix:** under the sandbox, refuse any control character in the raw payload's `file_path`, before `$(...)` or sed can change it.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3dac28e91bef916382c65042687598ddd3567ad0/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L843-L857
findings.suggestion:
const SYMLINK_CHECK_SHELL = `# Decision 191: sandboxed Bash can plant a symlink that this Edit or Write,
# outside the sandbox, would follow; no component of the path may be one.
# Checked on the raw payload: $(...) drops trailing newlines and sed rewrites
# per line, so a control character would make the walk test another path.
if printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -e '.tool_input.file_path | test("[[:cntrl:]]")' >/dev/null; then
  echo "BLOCKED: a path with a control character is refused under the worker sandbox." >&2; exit 2
fi
LINK_PATH=$WORKTREE

findings.description: The ADR calls its main-.git deny list "exactly these", but the list leaves out `hooks/`, which the code denies (`common('hooks')`, with its `.lock`). The `workerSandbox` JSDoc and docs/03-profiles.md leave it out too. Add `hooks/` to all three so whoever reconciles the list against the ADR doesn't remove it from the code.

`refs/stash` and `logs/refs/stash` in the main `.git` stay writable, so a worker can swap in a forged stash commit that the operator's next `git stash pop` applies to the main checkout. This is the same route as `MERGE_AUTOSTASH`, which is denied. A worker's own `git stash` writes these files, so they can't be denied; name the route in ADR 0191's writable list or ceilings instead.

process_issues.description: Round 4 budget: conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability were skipped per §4; spec skipped (no spec source); workflow-safety skipped (no workflow change).

Guards reviewer had `git ls-tree origin/main` denied (couldn't confirm ADR 0191 doesn't collide with a newer main ADR) and did not read the 29 candidate source-scanning guard tests, so a Linux-only guard failure is not ruled out.
